To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the language of sustainable development is increasingly evident in Watercare's reports; 2) the language of sustainability is used to construct meanings about the organization's environmental performance and the organization's role in society; and 3) the language of environmental sustainability is being replaced by the language of social sustainability.

Watercare Services Ltd's environmental and sustainable development reports are a good illustration of how organizations can change their reporting practices over time and, in so doing, change the ways that they construct their identity and the ways that they are seen by their stakeholders.
Watercare Services Ltd has developed a sustainable development discourse that is consistent and has evolved from a focus on environmental reporting to a focus on sustainable development reporting.
